To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel CPU-assisted GGPU approach to improve GPU memory access latency and performance on fused CPU-GPUs, by exploiting the CPU resource to pre-execute memory access instructions of GPU kernels.
our CPU-assisted GGPUP can significantly reduce the execution time of GPGPU applications on fused CPU-GPUs by utilizing the CPU resource to prefetch GPU memory accesses.
our CPU-assisted GPPU can improve the performance by up 113% and reduce the energy consumption by up to 28%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the CPU-assisted execution of GPU programs on fused CPU/GPU architectures.
a new paradigm of CPU-assisted GGPUs on fused CPU-GPUs, which can significantly improve the performance of GPGPU applications.

the following questions: How can we leverage the CPU resource on fused CPU-GPGPU architectures to facilitate the execution performance of GPGPU applications? Can the CPU be used to pre-execute memory accesses of GPU kernels? Can we automatically generate the pre-execution program from the original GPGPU kernel? Can the CPU pre-executed data be reused by the GPU kernel?

this paper presents a novel CPU-assisted GGPUGPU program execution model on fused CPU-GPUs.
this paper is about using the CPU to assist GPU execution on a shared memory system.
this paper proposes a novel approach to leverage CPU resources to facilitate GPGPU execution, and the proposed approach can improve the performance by up a factor of 2 on average.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CPU can be utilized to improve the performance of GPU programs on fused architectures.

the CPU-assisted GGP-GPU can significantly reduce the GPU kernel execution time by exploiting the CPU resource to prefetch data for GPU threads, and the performance improvement is not sensitive to the number of GPU threads.
we propose to utilize the CPU as a prefetcher for the GPU.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CPU and GPU are not mutually exclusive, and CPU can be used to assist GPU execution to improve the overall performance.
CPU can be used to facilitate the GPU execution on fused CPU-GPGPU architectures.
the CPU can be used to accelerate GPGPU programs by exploiting the memory hierarchy of the fused architectures.
